scope: Manual comparison of the 29 remaining interfaces (31 source members) in aos-2024-v52-i06-p2641 against the pinned mathlib revision, using frozen census statements and reviewed source distinctions; no PDF re-extraction or new theorem claims.

rows.query: Conditional expectation given a finite random-vector block; inspected comap and condExp with sigma-algebra, integrability and totalization conventions.
rows.result: Comap of the observation map omega -> (F_1(omega),...,F_T(omega)) supplies the conditioning sigma-algebra, and condExp supplies its conditional expectation. The usual meaning requires the sub-sigma-algebra and integrability obligations, rather than the definition's zero fallback.
rows.gap: These declarations express the notation after specifying the finite factor-block observation and verifying the conditional-expectation hypotheses.

comparisons.D17: Condition on the sigma-algebra generated by F_1,...,F_T, not on a deterministic signal or automatically on the entire integer-indexed factor process named separately in Assumption 1; equality of conditional versions is almost everywhere.

rows.query: Conditionally independent Gaussian tensor process, conditional laws and conditional quadratic second moments; inspected iCondIndepFun, IsGaussian, condDistrib and condExp.
rows.result: The indexed conditional-independence predicate covers mutual temporal independence and Gaussianity can be imposed on almost-everywhere conditional tensor laws. The uniform bound is a separate conditional integral inequality for every real vector. The inspected kernel-based infrastructure imposes standard Borel and finite-measure hypotheses.
rows.gap: The paper's error-process assumption still requires assembling conditional Gaussian laws, whole-process independence and the finite-block conditional second-moment inequality without adding centering or entrywise independence.

comparisons.D18: Use whole-process conditioning for the family of error tensors, but the source bar-E for the finite observed factor block in Ebar[(u^T vec(E_t))^2] <= sigma^2 ||u||_2^2, uniformly in u with sigma>0; this is neither the square of a conditional mean nor a centered covariance bound without an extra zero-mean argument, and no iid tensor entries are stated.

rows.query: TOPUP TIPUP iterative tensor factor algorithm, sequential coordinate update, mode products and least stopping index; inspected update, tensor-product map, L2 matrix norm and Nat.find.
rows.result: Coordinate update and tensor maps implement individual sweep steps; the Euclidean matrix operator norm expresses projector changes, and Nat.find can select a first stopping index once existence and the intended positive-index range are established. No TOPUP/TIPUP implementation was located in the pinned source search.
rows.gap: The full sequential sweep, initializer and iterator choices, finite stopping rule and four output families remain to be assembled and related to the theorem's iteration indices.

comparisons.D13: At sweep j, modes below k use freshly updated U_l^(j), modes above k use U_l^(j-1), and mode k is left unprojected; stop after a sweep at j=J or the maximum projector difference <= epsilon, then output U, UU^T, the projected core and X minus its all-mode projection, without inventing a constant continuation after stopping or silently assigning a J=0 convention.

rows.query: Tensor unfolding matricization and equivalent matrix index types; searched unfolding/matricization and inspected Matrix.reindex and its inverse submatrix maps.
rows.result: A finite tensor can be regrouped into one row index and a tuple of remaining indices, then reindex converts those tuple columns into a single finite index. It preserves entries but requires the actual equivalences to be supplied.
rows.gap: The paper's unfolding is expressible by finite index regrouping and reindexing once its cyclic one-based column formulas are implemented.

comparisons.D3: Retain shape m_k by product_{j!=k} m_j and, for order three, columns j+m_2(k-1), k+m_3(i-1), and i+m_1(j-1) in modes 1,2,3 respectively; a generic lexicographic flattening does not automatically reproduce all three cyclic conventions.

rows.query: Noiseless lagged matricized inner-product average; inspected matrix multiplication and coordinatewise finite sums with a common denominator.
rows.result: Matrix multiplication contracts the non-k indices, and entrywise finite sums/division supply the lag average, with transpose selecting the matching columns.
rows.gap: These operations suffice to define the noiseless matrix average once the paper's unfolding and the valid lag range h<T are supplied.

comparisons.D20: Define the d_k by d_k matrix sum_{t=h+1}^T mat_k(M_{t-h}) mat_k(M_t)^T/(T-h), keeping the ordered lagged pair and uncentered entries; it is a matrix contraction, not the order-four outer product Theta_{k,h}.

rows.query: Tensor-factor lower-bound distribution class, independent component time series, iid Gaussian noise, lag moments and singular-value restrictions; inspected family independence, Gaussian laws, integrals, tensor maps and singularValues.
rows.result: These declarations represent the tensor model, independent component processes and core/noise blocks, scalar Gaussian noise laws and uncentered moment matrices. The class is a conjunction of model-specific restrictions; a generic Gaussian tensor or factor-model definition does not imply them.
rows.gap: The restricted distribution class still needs its orthonormal loadings, independent component-series laws, lag-one moment constraint and singular-value convention assembled explicitly.

comparisons.D32: This is a class of data laws, with U_k^T U_k=I, mean-zero component series independent across component indices but not across time, their average lag-one expectation c_0>0, and all time-entry errors iid N(0,sigma^2) independent of the core process; use T>1 for the displayed denominator and preserve the source's smallest nontrivial singular-value convention instead of inferring full rank from c_1>0.

rows.query: Order-four tensor bilinear operator norm on two Hilbert-Schmidt unit matrices; inspected matrix L2 operator norm, Euclidean norm and finite index reindexing.
rows.result: Flattening the first index pair and the last index pair gives a real rectangular matrix between Euclidean spaces whose vector norms are the two Hilbert-Schmidt norms. Sign symmetry of real unit vectors removes the apparent missing absolute value; compactness and nonempty spheres give maximum attainment in positive dimensions.
rows.gap: The remaining work is the flattening and maximum-equals-operator-norm proof with nonempty unit spheres for the paper's two-matrix contraction.

comparisons.D7: The two U variables are independently optimized unit Hilbert-Schmidt matrices, even though their entries share the letter u; this is a two-block bilinear norm, not a four-vector injective norm or a same-vector quadratic form, and no symmetry or positive semidefiniteness of the order-four tensor is assumed.

rows.query: Tensor outer product with coefficient A_i B_j; inspected vecMulVec, its entry equation and comparison with algebraic tensor-product and Kronecker representations.
rows.result: With row index equal to the complete multi-index of A and column index equal to that of B, vecMulVec has exactly the required coefficient product; regrouping the indices gives the order-K+N array.
rows.gap: The existing outer-product operation suffices after identifying the two multi-index blocks with the concatenated tensor indices.

comparisons.D4: Retain all K indices of A followed by all N indices of B and entries A_i B_j, with no contracted indices; the source's tensor outer product must not be replaced by a matrix Kronecker product under an unrecorded row/column ordering.

rows.query: TIPUP matrix lagged inner products and horizontal concatenation; searched TIPUP and inspected mul_apply, sum_apply and fromCols.
rows.result: Finite matrix products and averages form each lag block; repeated horizontal concatenation or equivalent paired column indices assemble the d_k by d_k h_0 matrix.
rows.gap: The TIPUP matrix can be assembled from these operations with the paper's unfolding, lag normalization and column order.

comparisons.D12: Use mat_k(X_{t-h}) mat_k(X_t)^T/(T-h), summed from h+1 to T, and concatenate h=1,...,h_0; there is no mean subtraction, tensor outer product, or SVD in this matrix-valued definition itself.

rows.query: TIPUP estimator and truncated left singular matrix of concatenated lag contractions; inspected matrix blocks, symmetric eigenvectorBasis and ordered singularValues.
rows.result: The lag matrix is composable, and a leading eigenbasis of its left Gram operator supplies candidate left singular vectors. Singular values alone do not choose an m-column estimator or settle tie and measurable-selection conventions.
rows.gap: The TIPUP operator still needs its lag matrix and truncated left singular-vector selection assembled with the source's rank and tie conventions.

comparisons.D36: Apply LSVD_m to the d_k by d_k h_0 concatenated inner-product matrix, retaining m as the operator's supplied truncation argument; do not force m=r_k outside the algorithm call or claim that an arbitrary noncomputable eigenbasis provides a measurable data-to-estimator map.

rows.query: iTIPUP initialization and iteration, sequential tensor projection and spectral update; searched iTIPUP/TIPUP and inspected coordinate update, tensor map and Gram eigenbasis.
rows.result: The primitives support the generic projected sweep and its spectral step, but the pinned search did not locate the assembled iTIPUP procedure.
rows.gap: iTIPUP requires instantiating both slots of the source's sequential algorithm with the TIPUP operator and preserving its stopping rule.

comparisons.D15: Both INIT and ITER must be TIPUP, using the inner-product lag matrix on the original series at initialization and on the sequentially projected series thereafter; neither slot is TOPUP.

rows.query: Hypergraphic planted clique, uniform m-hypergraph, independent Bernoulli edges and uniform fixed-size subset; searched planted clique and inspected Hypergraph, powersetCard, Bernoulli, product measure and finite uniform PMF.
rows.result: Hypergraph supplies set-valued edges; m-element subsets index independent fair edge indicators, while the nonempty finite type of kappa-subsets supports uniform clique selection. An independent product and the edge-union map assemble the planted law; no complete HPC law was located.
rows.gap: The null and planted distributions and symmetric adjacency encoding still require assembling the independent edge law, uniform clique and edge-union construction.

comparisons.D30: Index Bernoulli trials by unordered sets of m distinct vertices, so permuted tensor entries share one trial and repeated-vertex tuples are not edges; sample the kappa-subset uniformly without replacement and independently of the null graph, requiring a nonempty subset family such as 0<=kappa<=N, before adjoining every m-edge contained in it.

rows.query: HPC computational hardness hypothesis, polynomial-time binary tests and limsup testing risk; searched planted clique and inspected TM2ComputableInPolyTime, limsup, log and event probabilities.
rows.result: The deterministic encoded-machine structure represents one precise notion of polynomial computation, and limsup/log/probability express the numerical claim. They do not establish the conjectured testing lower bound or automatically identify the source's test-family and randomized-computation conventions.
rows.gap: The HPC hardness assertion remains an assumption requiring explicit test encodings and quantifier conventions, rather than a consequence of the existing polynomial-time and probability definitions.

comparisons.D31: Preserve fixed m>=2, the displayed limsup log(kappa)/log(N)<=1/2-delta 'for any delta>0', and limsup of type-I plus type-II risk strictly >1/2 for every polynomial-time test sequence; do not replace limsup by liminf, turn the hypothesis into a proved theorem, or silently reconcile the formal polynomial-time wording with surrounding randomized-polynomial-time prose.

rows.query: Lagged uncentered tensor outer-product average, noiseless unfolding and canonical mode projections; inspected outer-product entries, finite function sums/division and tensor-product maps.
rows.result: Outer products on complete multi-indices and finite coordinatewise averages express all three variants; tensor maps implement the canonical all-mode projection. Their different input tensors and index shapes remain explicit.
rows.gap: These operations suffice to construct the three lag averages after supplying their unfolding and canonical projection maps with h<T.

comparisons.D9: Average X_{t-h} tensor-outer-product X_t from t=h+1 to T with denominator T-h, producing an order-2K tensor with the full d-index block repeated; the sample expression is uncentered despite its autocovariance naming.
comparisons.D19: Average the outer products of mat_k(M_{t-h}) and mat_k(M_t), with shape (d_k,d_-k,d_k,d_-k); retain noiseless M and all four indices instead of contracting the non-k modes as in Theta-star.
comparisons.D33: First project each noiseless M in every mode by U_l^T from the loading SVD, then unfold mode k and average outer products with shape (r_k,r_-k,r_k,r_-k); these canonical coordinates need not equal the original F coordinates unless the remaining loading factors are accounted for.

rows.query: Canonical lagged inner-product matrix, U-transpose Theta U and projected tensor contraction; inspected matrix multiplication, tensor maps and finite sums.
rows.result: Both displayed formulas are expressible with these operations. Their equality uses orthonormal loading-space coordinates and the fact that the noiseless tensor lies in the loading spaces for every mode.
rows.gap: The canonical inner-product construction still needs the loading-space identity proving its two source representations agree.

comparisons.D34: Keep the r_k by r_k matrix U_k^T Theta-star_{k,h} U_k and the average of products of all-mode projected noiseless M unfoldings; the non-k projection factors disappear only through signal subspace membership, so the identity must not be asserted for arbitrary noisy X.

rows.query: TIPUP signal strength, conditional noiseless lag matrices and m-th singular value; inspected ordered singularValues, conditional expectation, square root and real powers.
rows.result: The rank-indexed singular value and nested h_0 scaling are available operations. Equality between the conditional observed matrix, noiseless concatenation and canonical concatenation requires statistical cancellation and isometry arguments, not just notation.
rows.gap: The starred strength still needs the conditional-noise and canonical-isometry identities, with positivity proved separately before reciprocal rates are interpreted.

comparisons.D22: Translate source m-th singular value to zero-based index m-1, retain the three displayed tau-star representations and lambda-star=sqrt(h_0^(-1/2) tau-star_{k,r_k}); lag contraction may cancel signal so lambda-star may vanish, and it cannot be identified with the unstarred TOPUP strength by generic singular-value infrastructure.

rows.query: TIPUP initial risk formula with reciprocal signal strength, square-root dimensions and matrix operator norm; inspected sqrt, rpow and L2 operator norm.
rows.result: Existing real arithmetic and the Euclidean matrix norm express the displayed rate once the starred strength and noiseless lag-zero matrix are supplied; they do not prove a risk inequality.
rows.gap: The rate expression is composable from these operations on its intended positive T and nonzero starred-strength domain.

comparisons.D27: Retain (lambda-star)^(-2) sigma T^(-1/2) sqrt(d_k) times (||Theta-star_{k,0}||_S^(1/2)+sigma sqrt(d_-k)), where d_-k is the product of non-k dimensions; the dimension factor is outside the parentheses and no squared-rate correction occurs.

rows.query: TOPUP horizontal concatenation of matricized tensor lag averages; searched TOPUP and inspected outer products, reindexing, column concatenation and finite sums.
rows.result: The tensor lag average and its unfolding can be represented by finite arrays; concatenation creates the full lag matrix. The outer-product columns retain both full tensor index blocks apart from the selected row mode.
rows.gap: These operations can assemble TOPUP after fixing the source's unfolding and lag-column ordering.

comparisons.D10: Concatenate mat_k(Sigma-hat_h) for h=1,...,h_0 into a d_k by (d d_-k h_0) matrix, with d the product of all dimensions and d_-k=d/d_k on positive dimensions; preserve the outer-product average and do not substitute TIPUP's contracted d_k h_0 columns.

rows.query: TOPUP conditional signal strength and canonical noiseless singular-value equalities; inspected singularValues, conditional expectation and real fractional powers.
rows.result: The scalar singular-value expression is available after constructing each matrix. Equality of their singular values requires the conditional-noise cancellation and loading isometries; the error assumption does not explicitly include conditional mean zero.
rows.gap: The unstarred strength still needs the source's conditional-noiseless and canonical singular-value identities justified under explicitly stated hypotheses.

comparisons.D21: Use the source m-th singular value via index m-1 for Ebar[TOPUP_k], mat_1(Theta_{k,1:h_0}) and mat_1(Phi-cano_{k,1:h_0}), then lambda_k=sqrt(h_0^(-1/2) tau_{k,r_k}); retain the outer-product construction, require positive h_0, and do not supply an unstated mean-zero assumption to certify the conditional identities.

rows.query: TOPUP additional error rate and non-k dimension-rank sum; inspected finite sums, sqrt and real powers.
rows.result: The dimension-rank sum and scalar rate are finite arithmetic expressions with the displayed positive-domain square root and reciprocal scalings.
rows.gap: These operations suffice to define the additional rate once the dimension-rank sum and nonzero signal-strength domain are specified.

comparisons.D26: Define d-star_-k as sum_{j!=k} d_j r_j, not a product, and retain lambda_k^(-2) sigma^2 T^(-1) (d-star_-k+sqrt(d-star_-k d_k r_-k)); the whole three-factor product belongs under this radical.

rows.query: TOPUP initial four-term rate, tensor bilinear norm and square-root dimension scalings; inspected sqrt, rpow and flattened L2 operator norm.
rows.result: The matrix norm and flattened order-four norm, together with real arithmetic, express the four terms. This is a definition of a rate quantity, not a consequence of generic norm estimates.
rows.gap: The expression is composable after supplying the source's two norm quantities, dimension products and positive reciprocal-scale domain.

comparisons.D23: Keep prefactor lambda^(-2) sigma T^(-1/2) and the four terms sqrt(d_k d_-k r_-k)||Theta-star||_S^(1/2), (sqrt(d_k)+sqrt(d_-k r))||Theta||_op^(1/2), sigma sqrt(d_k) d_-k, and sigma d_k sqrt(d_-k) T^(-1/2); in particular d_-k is outside the radical in the third term, and the two Theta norms are distinct.

rows.query: Sharper TOPUP R-script-k2 rate and explicit rank-dimension radical scopes; inspected real powers, sqrt and the two norms via matrix L2 infrastructure.
rows.result: The saved source expression is a finite arithmetic combination of supplied norm and signal quantities, requiring no new probability construction just to define it.
rows.gap: These operations suffice for the stated R-script-k2 expression once the source norm quantities and valid scale domain are supplied.

comparisons.D37: Preserve first factor sqrt(r_k) r_-k, second (sqrt(d_k)+sqrt(r r_-k))||Theta||_op^(1/2), third sigma(sqrt(d_k)+sqrt(r r_-k)), and fourth sigma sqrt(d_k) r T^(-1/2), all under the common lambda^(-2) sigma T^(-1/2) prefactor; r_-k in the first and r in the last term stay outside the radicals, and the proposition's guarantee is not part of this extracted definition.

rows.query: Ideal TOPUP rate, dimension-to-rank substitution and squared R-script-k1 correction; inspected sqrt, real powers and L2 norm representation.
rows.result: The explicit R-script-k1 formula and its squared correction are expressible in real arithmetic, retaining the source's separately defined R-script-k2.
rows.gap: The existing operations suffice to define the ideal rate with the explicit R-script-k1 formula and its squared correction.

comparisons.D25: Use R-ideal=R-script-k2+(R-script-k1)^2; in R-script-k1 the first and third dimension factors are sqrt(d_k) r_-k, the second is sqrt(d_k)+sqrt(r_-k r), and the last is sigma d_k sqrt(r_-k) T^(-1/2), with the common prefactor retained, so replacing non-k dimensions by ranks does not discard the correction or move r_-k under the first radical.

rows.query: TOPUP estimator as truncated left SVD of unfolded lag outer products; searched TOPUP and inspected column concatenation, reindexing, left-Gram eigenbasis and singular values.
rows.result: Matrix operations construct the lag matrix, and the symmetric spectral infrastructure supplies candidate leading left singular vectors. The paper-specific data-to-m-column operator is not already assembled by these declarations.
rows.gap: The TOPUP estimator still requires its outer-product lag matrix and truncated left singular-vector choice, including tie and measurability conventions.

comparisons.D35: Apply LSVD_m to the horizontally concatenated mat_k(Sigma-hat_h(X_1:T)) blocks, with the supplied truncation m; preserve d d_-k h_0 columns and distinguish the selected left vectors from the zero-based singular-value sequence and from TIPUP's contracted matrix.

rows.query: Starred ideal TIPUP rate with non-k rank noise term; inspected square root, real reciprocal powers and Euclidean matrix operator norm.
rows.result: This rate is directly expressible from the starred signal strength, lag-zero noiseless matrix norm and finite rank dimensions using the existing scalar operations.
rows.gap: The existing operations suffice to define the starred ideal rate on the intended positive T and nonzero signal-strength domain.

comparisons.D28: Retain (lambda-star)^(-2) sigma T^(-1/2) sqrt(d_k)(||Theta-star_{k,0}||_S^(1/2)+sigma sqrt(r_-k)); replace d_-k by r_-k only in the inner noise factor, and do not introduce the unstarred ideal rate's squared correction.

rows.query: TIPUP additional error as square-root dimension ratio times ideal rate; inspected square root and finite dimension-rank sums.
rows.result: A finite sum supplies d-star_-k, and square root, division and multiplication supply the factor applied to the already defined starred ideal rate.
rows.gap: These operations suffice to define the additional starred rate with d_k>0 and the source's dimension-rank sum.

comparisons.D29: Use sqrt(d-star_-k/d_k) R-star-ideal with d-star_-k=sum_{j!=k} d_j r_j; this is a multiplicative correction to the starred ideal rate, not the unstarred R-add formula or an additive term inside its square root.

rows.query: iTOPUP initializer and iterative outer-product spectral updates; searched iTOPUP/TOPUP and inspected sequential coordinate update, tensor projection maps and eigenbasis.
rows.result: The generic algebraic sweep and spectral ingredients are available, but the source's two-slot TOPUP algorithm is not provided as a complete implementation in the searched revision.
rows.gap: iTOPUP still needs both algorithm slots instantiated with TOPUP and the sequential projection and stopping behavior assembled.

comparisons.D14: Both initialization on the original series and every update on the projected series use the TOPUP outer-product operator, with no TIPUP substitution in either slot; the generic algorithm's fresh lower-mode and previous upper-mode updates remain in force.

rows.query: Mixed TIPUP-iTOPUP algorithm, inner-product initialization and outer-product iteration; searched algorithm names and inspected coordinate updates, tensor maps and spectral vectors.
rows.result: The operations support both spectral substeps and sequential projections, but selecting these two different operators is additional algorithm data.
rows.gap: The mixed procedure still needs TIPUP initialization followed by TOPUP sweeps with the source's shared stopping rule.

comparisons.D16: Set INIT to TIPUP and ITER to TOPUP, preserving their different lag-matrix shapes; do not merge the procedure with either unmixed algorithm or the reversed TOPUP-initialized TIPUP-iteration branch, which is not the branch used by Theorem 3.3.

rows.query: Sharper TOPUP rate as a supplied rate plus the square of the initial rate; inspected real-power definition and its integer-power interpretation.
rows.result: Existing real addition and squaring suffice to combine the two supplied rate quantities; no asymptotic or probability result is needed to define this scalar expression.
rows.gap: The existing arithmetic suffices for this definition once R-script-k2 and R-k-zero are supplied.

comparisons.D24: Define R-k-TOPUP=R-script-k2+(R-k-zero)^2, retaining the square of the original initial rate rather than R-script-k1; the small-initial-error premise of the surrounding proposition belongs to its guarantee and is not an additional hypothesis of this arithmetic definition.
